title: Immutable board store with filters and selection history (SPIDR: Data)
spec: Write src/store.ts. Import types with `import type { CanvasCard, CardClass, CardStatus, GateName, GateState } from "./tokens.js"` (relative imports end in .js). Export `export interface BoardFilter { text: string; cardClass: CardClass | null }`, `export interface BoardState { cards: CanvasCard[]; filter: BoardFilter; selectedId: string | null; history: string[] }`, `export type Action = { type: "addCard"; card: CanvasCard } | { type: "moveCard"; id: string; status: CardStatus } | { type: "updateGate"; id: string; gate: GateName; state: GateState } | { type: "select"; id: string | null } | { type: "back" } | { type: "setFilter"; filter: Partial<BoardFilter> }`, and `export const HISTORY_LIMIT = 10`. Export `export function createInitialState(cards: CanvasCard[] = []): BoardState` returning { cards: a copy of cards, filter: { text: "", cardClass: null }, selectedId: null, history: [] }. Export `export function reduce(state: BoardState, action: Action): BoardState`, a pure function that never mutates its input and returns the SAME state object when nothing changes: addCard appends, or throws new Error(`duplicate card: ${id}`); moveCard and updateGate replace the card with an updated copy, or throw new Error(`unknown card: ${id}`) for an unknown id, and return state unchanged when the status/gate already has that value; select throws `unknown card: ${id}` for an unknown non-null id, returns state unchanged when id equals selectedId, otherwise sets selectedId and, if the previous selectedId was not null, appends it to history keeping only the last HISTORY_LIMIT entries; back pops the last history entry into selectedId, or returns state unchanged when history is empty; setFilter merges the partial filter into filter. Export `export function visibleCards(state: BoardState): CanvasCard[]` keeping cards whose lower-cased title contains the trimmed, lower-cased filter text (empty text matches all) and whose cardClass equals filter.cardClass when that is not null. Export `export interface Store { getState(): BoardState; dispatch(action: Action): void; subscribe(listener: (state: BoardState) => void): () => void }` and `export function createStore(initial: BoardState): Store`: dispatch runs reduce (letting errors propagate, leaving state unchanged), and only when the returned state is a different object stores it and calls every listener with it; subscribe returns an unsubscribe function.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. createInitialState() equals { cards: [], filter: { text: "", cardClass: null }, selectedId: null, history: [] }.
2. addCard with an existing id throws "duplicate card: x"; moveCard, updateGate and select with an unknown id throw "unknown card: zz".
3. reduce never mutates its input (a structuredClone snapshot still equals the old state) and returns the identical object for a no-op move or a back with empty history.
4. updateGate changes one gate of one card only.
5. Selecting a, b, c gives selectedId c and history [a, b]; back gives b and [a]; null and repeated selections are not recorded; history keeps only the last 10 ids.
6. Filter text "  PARSE " matches titles containing parse case-insensitively; text and cardClass filters combine.
7. Subscribers receive the new state, are not called for no-op actions, and stop receiving after unsubscribe; a throwing dispatch leaves getState() unchanged.
8. tests/store.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Kanban board columns, WIP badges, backpressure and virtualization (SPIDR: Visual)
spec:
Write src/board.ts. Import renderCardTile from "./card_tile.js" and types CanvasCard, CardStatus from "./tokens.js". Export `export const COLUMNS: CardStatus[] = ["backlog", "ready", "doing", "review", "done"]` and `export const WIP_LIMITS: Record = { backlog: null, ready: null, doing: 3, review: 2, done: null }`. Export `export interface ColumnModel { status: CardStatus; cards: CanvasCard[]; count: number; limit: number | null; overLimit: boolean; backpressure: boolean }` and `export function buildColumns(cards: CanvasCard[]): ColumnModel[]` returning one model per COLUMNS entry in order, with that status's cards in input order; overLimit is true only when limit is not null and count > limit; backpressure is true only for the review column when count >= its limit. Export `export interface ScrollViewport { scrollTop: number; height: number }` and `export function visibleRange(count: number, rowHeight: number, viewport: ScrollViewport, overscan = 2): { start: number; end: number }`: throw new RangeError("rowHeight must be positive") when rowHeight <= 0; return { start: 0, end: 0 } when count <= 0; otherwise start = max(0, floor(scrollTop / rowHeight) - overscan) and end = min(count, ceil((scrollTop + height) / rowHeight) + overscan), with start also capped at count. Export `export function renderColumnHeader(column: ColumnModel): string` returning the template literal `
${column.status}${badge}${warning}
` where badge is `${column.count}/${column.limit}`, or just `${column.count}` when limit is null; badgeClass is "wip-badge over-limit" when overLimit, else "wip-badge"; warning is 'Review is full' when backpressure, else the empty string. Export `export function renderBoard(cards: CanvasCard[], selectedId: string | null = null): string` returning '
' + for each column of buildColumns(cards) the template literal `
${renderColumnHeader(column)}${tiles}
` (tiles = the column's cards mapped to renderCardTile(card, { selected: card.id === selectedId }) and joined with "") + '
', with no whitespace between tags. This project is ESM with moduleResolution nodenext: any relative import must end in .js (for example from "./tokens.js").
acceptanceCriteria: 1. COLUMNS and WIP_LIMITS equal the values in the spec.
2. buildColumns groups cards by status in input order and counts them.
3. Doing with 3 cards is not overLimit; with 4 it is. Review with 1 card has no backpressure; with 2 it has backpressure and is not overLimit. No other column ever has backpressure.

4. visibleRange(1000, 40, { scrollTop: 400, height: 200 }) is { start: 8, end: 17 }; with overscan 0 it is { start: 10, end: 15 }; scrollTop 0 gives { start: 0, end: 7 }; count 10 at scrollTop 300 gives { start: 5, end: 10 }; count 0 gives { start: 0, end: 0 }.
5. visibleRange with rowHeight 0 or negative throws a RangeError with message "rowHeight must be positive".
6. Column headers render exactly as in the tests, including "wip-badge over-limit" 4/3 and the Review is full warning.
7. renderBoard renders five columns in order and exactly one is-selected tile for the selected id.
8. tests/board.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Layered DAG layout with longest-path ranks and bezier edges (SPIDR: Rule)
spec: Write src/dag_layout.ts. Import types DagEdge, DagNode from "./tokens.js". Export `export interface EdgeInput { from: string; to: string }` (from is the dependency, to depends on it), `export interface LayoutOptions { nodeWidth?: number; nodeHeight?: number; rankGap?: number; nodeGap?: number }` and `export interface DagLayout { nodes: DagNode[]; edges: DagEdge[]; width: number; height: number }`. Export `export function computeRanks(ids: string[], edges: EdgeInput[]): Map<string, number>`: first, any edge endpoint not in ids throws new Error(`unknown node: ${id}`) (check from before to); rank is 0 for a node with no incoming edge, otherwise 1 + the maximum rank of its predecessors (longest path); any cycle, including a self-loop, throws new Error("cycle detected") (use a depth-first search with a visiting set). Export `export function bezierPath(x1: number, y1: number, x2: number, y2: number): string` returning `M x1 y1 C mx y1 mx y2 x2 y2` with mx = (x1 + x2) / 2 and single spaces, numbers formatted by template literals. Export `export function layoutDag(ids: string[], edges: EdgeInput[], options: LayoutOptions = {}): DagLayout` with defaults nodeWidth 160, nodeHeight 40, rankGap 80, nodeGap 24: nodes are returned in ids order; order is the count of earlier ids with the same rank; x = rank * (nodeWidth + rankGap); y = order * (nodeHeight + nodeGap); width and height of every node are nodeWidth and nodeHeight. Edges are returned in input order with path = bezierPath(from.x + nodeWidth, from.y + nodeHeight / 2, to.x, to.y + nodeHeight / 2). Layout width = rankCount * nodeWidth + (rankCount - 1) * rankGap and height = rows * nodeHeight + (rows - 1) * nodeGap where rankCount is the highest rank + 1 and rows is the largest number of nodes in one rank; an empty graph returns { nodes: [], edges: [], width: 0, height: 0 }. This project is ESM with moduleResolution nodenext: any relative import must end in .js (for example from "./tokens.js").
acceptanceCriteria: 1. The diamond a->b, a->c, b->d, c->d ranks { a: 0, b: 1, c: 1, d: 2 }; with a->c, a->b, b->c the rank of c is 2 (longest path).
2. Isolated nodes have rank 0; a two-node cycle and a self-loop throw "cycle detected"; an edge to ghost throws "unknown node: ghost".
4. The diamond layout places c at x 240, y 64 and d at x 480, y 0, with width 640 and height 104.
5. Edge paths start at the source's right middle and end at the target's left middle.
6. Custom options are honoured; an empty graph has width 0 and height 0; one node has width 160 and height 40.
7. tests/dag_layout.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: DAG canvas pan, zoom, hit testing and SVG rendering (SPIDR: Visual)
spec: Write src/dag_canvas.ts. Import escapeHtml from "./card_tile.js" and `import type { DagLayout } from "./dag_layout.js"`. Export `export interface Point { x: number; y: number }`, `export interface Viewport { x: number; y: number; scale: number }` (screen = world * scale + offset), `export const MIN_SCALE = 0.25` and `export const MAX_SCALE = 4`. Export `export function worldToScreen(v: Viewport, p: Point): Point` and `export function screenToWorld(v: Viewport, p: Point): Point` (screen to world is (p - offset) / scale). Export `export function pan(v: Viewport, dx: number, dy: number): Viewport` returning a new viewport offset by dx, dy. Export `export function zoomAt(v: Viewport, factor: number, anchor: Point): Viewport`: throw new RangeError("zoom factor must be positive") unless factor > 0 (so NaN is rejected too); new scale = v.scale * factor clamped to MIN_SCALE..MAX_SCALE; the world point under the screen anchor must stay under it, so new x = anchor.x - world.x * newScale and likewise for y, where world = screenToWorld(v, anchor). Export `export function hitTest(layout: DagLayout, v: Viewport, screen: Point): string | null` converting the point to world space and returning the id of the LAST node in layout.nodes that contains it (x <= px < x + width and y <= py < y + height), or null. Export `export function renderDagSvg(layout: DagLayout, v: Viewport, selectedId: string | null): string` returning these template literals concatenated with no whitespace: `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${layout.width}" height="${layout.height}">`, `<g transform="translate(${v.x} ${v.y}) scale(${v.scale})">`, then for each edge `<path class="edge" d="${edge.path}"/>`, then for each node (with id = escapeHtml(node.id) and cls = "node is-selected" when node.id === selectedId, else "node") `<g class="${cls}" data-id="${id}"><rect x="${node.x}" y="${node.y}" width="${node.width}" height="${node.height}" rx="4"/><text x="${node.x + 8}" y="${node.y + node.height / 2}">${id}</text></g>`, then "</g></svg>". This project is ESM with moduleResolution nodenext: any relative import must end in .js (for example from "./tokens.js").
acceptanceCriteria: 1. With viewport { x: 10, y: 10, scale: 2 }, world (50, 10) maps to screen (110, 30) and back.
2. pan returns a new viewport and does not mutate its input; MIN_SCALE is 0.25 and MAX_SCALE is 4.
3. zoomAt({ x: 0, y: 0, scale: 1 }, 2, { x: 100, y: 50 }) is { x: -100, y: -50, scale: 2 } and the anchor maps to itself; scales clamp to 4 and 0.25.
4. zoomAt with factor 0, -2 or NaN throws RangeError "zoom factor must be positive".
5. hitTest returns the topmost (last) overlapping node, includes left/top edges, excludes right/bottom edges, and returns null for empty space or an empty layout.
6. renderDagSvg matches the exact markup in the test, marks only the selected node, and escapes ids.
7. tests/dag_canvas.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: Accessible Cmd+K command palette with fuzzy search (SPIDR: Visual)
spec:
Write src/palette.ts. Import escapeHtml from "./card_tile.js". Export `export interface PaletteItem { id: string; label: string; kind: "card" | "dependency" | "setting" }`, `export interface PaletteState { open: boolean; query: string; items: PaletteItem[]; results: PaletteItem[]; activeIndex: number }` and `export type PaletteKey = "Mod+K" | "Escape" | "ArrowDown" | "ArrowUp" | "Enter"`. Export `export function fuzzyScore(query: string, label: string): number | null`: compare lower-cased strings; walk the query characters left to right, finding each at the earliest label index after the previous match (greedy indexOf); return null if any is missing; each matched character scores 1, plus 2 if its index is exactly the previous match's index + 1, plus 3 if its index is 0 or the preceding label character is a space, "-" or "_"; the empty query scores 0. Export `export function search(items: PaletteItem[], query: string): PaletteItem[]`: for the empty query return all items sorted by label ascending (plain < comparison); otherwise drop items with a null score and sort by score descending, then label ascending. Export `export function createPalette(items: PaletteItem[]): PaletteState` (closed, query "", results = search(items, ""), activeIndex 0) and `export function setQuery(state: PaletteState, query: string): PaletteState` (new query, recomputed results, activeIndex 0). Export `export function paletteKey(state: PaletteState, key: PaletteKey): { state: PaletteState; chosen: PaletteItem | null }`: Mod+K closes an open palette, or opens a closed one with query reset to "" (results for "" and activeIndex 0); while closed every other key returns the state unchanged with chosen null; Escape closes; ArrowDown and ArrowUp move activeIndex by one, wrapping around, and do nothing when there are no results; Enter returns chosen = results[activeIndex] and closes, or chosen null and stays open when there are no results. Export `export function renderPalette(state: PaletteState): string` returning "" when closed. When open, let active = state.results[state.activeIndex] and activeAttr = active ? ` aria-activedescendant="opt-${escapeHtml(active.id)}"` : "" (note the leading space), and return these template literals concatenated with no whitespace: `
    `, then for each result at index i `
  • ${escapeHtml(item.label)}
    • `, then "
". This project is ESM with moduleResolution nodenext: any relative import must end in .js (for example from "./tokens.js").
acceptanceCriteria: 1. fuzzyScore("abc", "abc") is 10, ("gt", "gate strip") is 5, ("gs", "gate strip") is 8, ("GS", "Gate Strip") is 8, ("", "anything") is 0.
2. fuzzyScore returns null for "xyz", "pg" against "gate strip" and for "gates" against "gate"; "b" scores 4 in "a-b" and "a_b" but 1 in "a.b".
3. search sorts by score descending then label ascending; the empty query returns every item sorted by label; no match returns [].
4. Mod+K opens with every item and activeIndex 0, Mod+K or Escape closes, and reopening resets the query.
5. ArrowDown/ArrowUp wrap in both directions; changing the query resets activeIndex to 0.
6. Enter returns the active item and closes; with no results it returns null and stays open; closed palettes ignore every key except Mod+K.
7. renderPalette returns "" when closed and the exact dialog/combobox/listbox markup in the test when open; aria-activedescendant is omitted when there are no results; the query is escaped.
8. tests/palette.spec.ts passes without modification.

title: WCAG contrast audit, drag and click transitions, full app render (SPIDR: Integration)
spec: Write src/app.ts. Imports (relative imports end in .js): WIP_LIMITS, renderBoard from "./board.js"; layoutDag and type DagLayout from "./dag_layout.js"; reduce, visibleCards and type BoardState from "./store.js"; types CanvasCard, CardStatus, ThemeTokens from "./tokens.js". Export `export function contrastRatio(foreground: string, background: string): number` implementing WCAG 2.1: each color must match /^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$/ else throw new Error(`invalid color: ${color}`); channel c = hex pair / 255, linearised as c <= 0.03928 ? c / 12.92 : ((c + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4; luminance = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B; ratio = (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05) rounded to 2 decimals with Math.round(ratio * 100) / 100. Export `export interface ContrastCheck { pair: string; ratio: number; required: number; pass: boolean }` and `export function auditTheme(theme: ThemeTokens): ContrastCheck[]` returning, in this order, text pairs requiring 4.5: textPrimary on bgBase, bgSurface, bgRaised, bgOverlay, then textMuted on bgBase, bgSurface, bgRaised; then accent pairs requiring 3: gold, nile, ochre, lapis each on bgRaised. pair is "foreground/background" using the token names (for example "textPrimary/bgBase") and pass is ratio >= required. Export `export interface DragResult { state: BoardState; ok: boolean; reason: string | null }` and `export function dragCard(state: BoardState, id: string, to: CardStatus): DragResult`, checking in this order: unknown id -> { state, ok: false, reason: `unknown card: ${id}` }; card already in `to` -> { state, ok: true, reason: null }; WIP_LIMITS[to] not null and the number of cards already in `to` >= that limit -> reason `WIP limit reached for ${to}`; moving to "doing" while any id in card.dependsOn is not a card with status "done" -> reason `blocked by ${firstSuchId}`; otherwise { state: reduce(state, { type: "moveCard", id, status: to }), ok: true, reason: null }. Failed drags return the original state object. Export `export function clickCard(state: BoardState, id: string): BoardState` dispatching select with null when id is already selected (toggle off), else id. Export `export function buildDag(cards: CanvasCard[]): DagLayout` calling layoutDag(card ids in order, edges { from: dependency, to: card.id } for each card and each of its dependsOn in order). Export `export function renderApp(state: BoardState): string` returning `<main class="app">` + renderBoard(visibleCards(state), state.selectedId) + `</main>`.
acceptanceCriteria: 1. contrastRatio("#000000", "#FFFFFF") is 21 in either order, ("#777777", "#FFFFFF") is 4.48, a color on itself is 1, lower-case hex works, and "#FFF" throws "invalid color: #FFF".
2. auditTheme(THEME) returns the eleven checks in the listed order with the exact ratios in the test, all passing.
3. With textMuted "#3A362F" exactly the three textMuted pairs fail.

4. dragCard moves a card whose dependencies are done; returns { state, ok: false, reason: "blocked by tile" } for an unmet dependency; reports "WIP limit reached for review" when Review holds 2 cards; reports "unknown card: ghost"; treats a same-column drop as ok with the same state.
5. clickCard selects, and a second click on the same card deselects with history ["tile"].
6. renderApp wraps the filtered board in <main class="app"> and marks the selected tile.
7. buildDag lays out cards by dependsOn with the exact ranks, orders and coordinates in the test; a dependency on a missing card throws "unknown node: missing".
8. tests/e2e_ui.spec.ts passes without modification.
